samples.summary: Three (arguably four) independent concerns are bundled in one change: (a) OAuth loopback nonce binding + `/start` indirection in `login`/backend, (b) a new URL path-segment encoding/rejection layer (`client/url.ts`) applied across the whole client, (c) `--dry-run` support on read commands and `api-keys`, and (d) an unrelated fix to the `scripts/test/changed-areas.test.mjs` push-to-main fall-through assertion. Each has its own design-doc section and its own risk profile; (d) touches CI lane selection and has nothing to do with the CLI or auth. Bundling makes the fit of any one piece hard to judge and hard to revert independently.
samples.evidence: The diff spans packages/backend/src/auth/* (nonce echo), packages/cli/src/client/url.ts (traversal rejection), ~10 command files (dry-run on reads), and scripts/test/changed-areas.test.mjs (CI lane resolution test), with three separate design-doc sections updated (cli.md §3.1, cli.md §8.2, rest-api.md risk table).

samples.summary: The new user-facing `login --allow-unbound-callback` flag is not reflected in the CLI's self-describing surfaces: it is absent from the `schema` registry entry for `login` (packages/cli/src/schema/registry.ts:43-50, which lists only `--server`) and from the canonical Command Tree in docs/design/cli.md §4 (line 311, `login` shown with no options). "Self-describing schema" for agent consumption is a stated Goal of cli.md (§Goals, "structured output, self-describing schema, dry-run support"), and §4 is where every other command's flags are enumerated. The flag is only described in §3.1 prose.
samples.evidence: registry.ts:43-50 `parameters: { '--server': ... }` only; cli.md:311 `├── login  Browser OAuth login → writes session` with no bracketed options, unlike every other command line in the tree.

samples.summary: The change's own stated principle — "one definition used by both the live client and the `--dry-run` preview, so a preview cannot disagree with the request it describes" (client/url.ts) — is applied to path segments and the api-keys URL but NOT to the cells endpoint selection or the `?range=` query. `cells get`'s dry-run branch re-implements `HttpClient.getCells`/`getCell` endpoint choice (`range?.includes(':')`) and re-implements `?range=${encodeURIComponent(range)}` (also duplicated a third time in sheets-export.ts:49 and originally in http-client.ts:346). That is exactly the preview/request drift the new module exists to prevent; a shared `cellsPath()`/`cellsUrl()` builder in `client/url.ts` would have covered it.
samples.evidence: cells.ts:24-30 mirrors http-client.ts:346 and the get/getCell branch by hand; sheets-export.ts:47-53 duplicates the range query a third time; the doc even asserts "Mirrors `HttpClient.getCells` ... so the printed URL is the URL that would have been fetched", which is a hand-maintained invariant rather than a structural one.

samples.summary: The `/start` indirection changes the URL printed "for copy-paste in headless environments" from an absolute server URL (`https://<server>/auth/github?...`) to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/start`. A loopback URL is only meaningful on the machine running the CLI (or via an SSH-forwarded port); the previously printed absolute URL was at least openable from another machine even if the loopback callback then needed forwarding. The doc keeps advertising the printed URL as the headless copy-paste path without noting this narrowing, and cli.md's Non-Goals already list "Device flow or headless authentication" as out of scope — so the affordance being narrowed is one the design only half-supports.
samples.evidence: cli.md:175-177 "Opens (and prints, for copy-paste in headless environments) the nonce-free http://127.0.0.1:<port>/start"; login.ts prints `startUrl` instead of the authorize URL.

samples.summary: The `/start` one-shot redirect route adds a second local HTTP endpoint and a `setAuthorizeUrl` handshake to solve argv/stderr nonce exposure, while the design doc itself concedes the residual attack (a local process racing the browser to `/start`) is not closed and that the real fix is the deferred PKCE-shaped `POST /auth/cli/start`. Adding a second protocol surface for a partial mitigation, when the same doc says the complete mitigation is a separate backend endpoint "not part of this design yet", is arguably scope the issue did not ask for; the simpler shape (nonce on the printed authorize URL, PKCE next) would have kept the login flow to one route.
samples.evidence: cli.md:205-222 documents the `/start` hop and then "Closing even that needs the secret to never leave the CLI: a PKCE-shaped `POST /auth/cli/start` ... That endpoint is not part of this design yet"; rest-api.md risk table marks the PKCE mitigation "Not implemented".

finding.summary: Single-use `/start` is at odds with the documented headless copy-paste path it is supposed to preserve
finding.evidence: cli.md:176-178 now says step 3 "Opens (and prints, for copy-paste in headless environments) the nonce-free http://127.0.0.1:<port>/start", and cli.md:206-211 claims "the URL a headless user copies is the same one `open()` is given and the same one that works". Those two properties cannot both hold with a one-shot route: `login` always calls `open(startUrl)` (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:72) and only falls into the `catch` when the dynamic import or spawn itself throws — `open()` resolves normally in headless/CI environments where a launcher binary exists (xdg-open, `start`, wslview) but no browser ever renders, and browsers can also issue more than one request to a URL (prefetch/preconnect, restored tab). In those cases the first `GET /start` consumes the nonce and the URL the CLI just told the user to visit ("If the browser does not open, visit the URL above.", login.ts:68) answers `410 START_CONSUMED_MESSAGE`, leaving the invocation with no way to complete — a regression against the prior behaviour, which printed a URL that still worked when the browser did not appear. The design doc asserts the property rather than reconciling it (e.g. allowing re-issue until the callback arrives, or only arming single-use after a successful open).

verdict.reason: The cited code and doc text exist exactly as claimed. login.ts:266-281 makes GET /start strictly one-shot (startConsumed set on first hit, 410 START_CONSUMED_MESSAGE thereafter, no re-arm and no re-issue while the callback is pending), while login.ts:67-68 prints that same one-shot URL as the headless fallback ("If the browser does not open, visit the URL above.") and login.ts:70-75 always calls open(startUrl), reaching the catch only when the import/spawn itself throws — so a launcher that resolves without rendering a usable browser, or any duplicate/speculative hit, spends the single use and leaves the printed URL answering 410 with no way to finish the invocation. docs/design/cli.md:175-177 and 206-218 assert the property that the copied URL is "the same one open() is given and the same one that works", reconciling single-use only against the racing-local-process threat model and deferring the rest to a future PKCE endpoint; the benign consumption case is asserted away rather than designed for (no re-issue until callback, no arm-after-successful-open). No guard elsewhere makes this unreachable, and it is not merely a line-level logic nit: it is a design-doc claim about a documented user path that the implementation cannot uphold, and the same /start single-use defect is independently recorded as a confirmed major by the correctness lane, so I have no named ground to drop it.
